summary: A target-level continuation of the accepted ArithmeticKTheory N.1 packet. Retain its rank filtration, coefficient conventions and number-field/S-integer endpoints by ID. Five fresh refinements give the shifted relative homology comparison, degreewise rank stability, integral finite type of Q homology, the H-space/Serre passage to K-groups, and finite defects of finite-S localization. Building and arithmetic duality remain owned by Borel R.1 and its ALS suppliers. Coverage is planned with explicit homotopy supplier and signature gaps; no implementation is claimed.

nodes.title: Relative homology of a rank layer
nodes.statement: Let A be a Dedekind domain with fraction field F, and m ≥ 1. For every integer i ≥ 0 there is a natural integral comparison H_i(BQ_m(A), BQ_{m−1}(A); Z) ≅ ⊕_[P],rank(P)=m H_{i−m}(Aut_A(P); St(P⊗_A F)). Group homology in negative degrees is zero. Relative homology is that of the mapping cone of the inclusion on integral chains. The comparison intertwines the relative long exact sequence with Quillen’s Theorem 3; it is independent of chosen representatives up to the induced coefficient isomorphisms.
hypotheses: Use the rank filtration and its comma-category/building identifications from the predecessor; do not construct a second Q-category or building.
St(V)=Z with trivial action in rank one. For m≥2 it is reduced H_{m−2} of the ordinary building.
Indices i−m are integers, not truncated subtraction of natural numbers.
proofSteps: Apply Kahn 2.3.7 to the cellular inclusion Q_{m−1} → Q_m. Its complement is the groupoid of rank-m projectives (predecessor rank-filtration).

The augmented reduced chain complex of each comma category has homology concentrated in degree m−1, with coefficient St(P⊗F), by the predecessor suspended-building comparison. Its group hyperhomology collapses to H_{i−m}(Aut P;St). Include the extra mapping-cone shift [1].

Decompose groupoid homology over projective isomorphism classes. Use the functorial mapping-cone comparison in Kahn 4.3.4 for m≥2; for m=1 use 2.3.7 with the explicit augmented chains of two points, rather than its positive-sphere-dimension argument.
acceptance: For i<m the right side and relative group are zero.
For m=1 and i=1 the right side is a direct sum of copies of Z, one per Pic(A); the Aut action on St is trivial.
For m=2 and i=2 the term is Steinberg coinvariants H_0, not ordinary H_0(Aut P;Z) or the free module on all lines.

sources.match: The reduced coefficient complex and mapping-cone shift identify relative homology, including rank one.
The exact sequence is the relative sequence with the stated shift.

nodes.title: Homological stability of the Q rank filtration
nodes.statement: For a Dedekind domain A and integers i,n ≥ 0, H_i(BQ_n(A);Z) → H_i(BQ_{n+1}(A);Z) is surjective for n≥i and an isomorphism for n≥i+1. The canonical map H_i(BQ_n(A);Z) → H_i(BQ(A);Z) has the same surjectivity bound and is an isomorphism for n≥i+1. These are rank-filtration bounds, not stable-range assertions for H_i(GL_n(A);Z).
hypotheses: Integral coefficients; no finite-Pic or arithmetic hypothesis is required.
The filtration is exhaustive on finite simplices, with homology commuting with its filtered union.
proofSteps: At the step adding rank n+1, the relative groups in degrees i and i+1 vanish respectively for n≥i and n≥i+1 by relative-rank-homology-comparison. Apply the relative long exact sequence.

Every simplex uses finitely many projectives and lies in some Q_n; every finite chain and relation therefore lies at finite rank. Use H.1’s filtered-union comparison to identify homology of the union with its filtered colimit.
All later transition maps are isomorphisms once n≥i+1. This proves stabilization to BQ without any general assertion that a colimit of finitely generated groups is finitely generated.
acceptance: At n=i only surjectivity is asserted; the relative term in degree i+1 may be nonzero.
For i=0, Q_0 and BQ are connected and the map on H_0 is Z → Z.
There is no claimed fixed-rank bound simultaneously for every homological degree.

sources.match: The printed bounds are n≥i for surjectivity and n≥i+1 for injectivity.

nodes.title: Integral finite type of the rank-filtered Q-space
nodes.statement: Let A be a Dedekind domain with fraction field F. Assume Pic(A) is finite and H_q(Aut_A(P);St(P⊗_A F)) is a finitely generated abelian group for every finite projective P of positive rank and every q≥0. Then all H_i(BQ_n(A);Z), for i,n≥0, and all H_i(BQ(A);Z) are finitely generated abelian groups. For A=O_F, both hypotheses are supplied by the baseline class-group theorem, the LowDegrees Pic comparison, and BorelRegulators:R.1/steinberg-duality-finiteness for all projective lattices, including nonfree ones.
hypotheses: Steinberg homology is assumed integrally, in every degree, for every projective isomorphism class; ordinary arithmetic homology is insufficient.
Positive-rank projective classes are parametrized by Pic(A); rank zero has one class.
proofSteps: By the predecessor Steinitz/classification and rank-filtration nodes, each positive rank has finitely many projective isomorphism classes. Relative-rank-homology-comparison makes every relative group a finite direct sum of finitely generated abelian groups.

Start with Q_0 equivalent to the terminal category, so H_0=Z and higher homology vanishes. Induct on n using the relative long exact sequence. The middle absolute group is an extension of a quotient of the previous absolute group by a subgroup of the relative group. Subgroups of finitely generated abelian groups are finitely generated; use Z-module Noetherianity and the baseline exact-sequence finiteness lemma.
For fixed i choose n=i+1 and apply rank-homology-stability. This avoids the invalid passage from arbitrary finite-type stages to finite-type colimit.

For O_F identify Pic with ClassGroup by LowDegrees. Import the Borel node for the actual lattice P, not only GL_m(O_F). Its proof uses orientation-correct integral duality on a normal torsion-free subgroup and integral finite-quotient descent.
acceptance: For O_F with class number greater than one, all Steinitz classes contribute; keeping only free lattices fails the hypothesis.
Finite rational dimension of the coefficient homology does not imply this integral statement.
An infinite direct sum of copies of Z is not finitely generated; finite Pic is used before summing.

sources.locator: Proof of Theorem 1, printed pp.184–185, PDF pp.192–193
sources.match: Induction over finite rank and degreewise stabilization yield integral finite generation.
The criterion requires finite Pic and integral Steinberg-coefficient homology.

nodes.title: From integral homology to finitely generated K-groups
nodes.statement: Under the two hypotheses of rank-filtration-homology-finite-type, K_n(A)=π_{n+1}(BQ(P(A)),0) is a finitely generated abelian group for every n≥0. In particular this holds for O_F for every number field F. Direct sum makes the connected CW-type space BQ(P(A)) a homotopy associative and commutative H-space, hence a simple space, so the integral Serre finite-type theorem applies. This supplies the proof interface of the retained quillen-finiteness-criterion and quillen-finite-generation-theorem; it does not replace the K-group carrier.
hypotheses: CW type is furnished by nerve realization, with basepoint the zero projective.
Simple means π_1 is abelian and its action on each higher homotopy group is trivial; simple does not mean simply connected.
The general Serre theorem is a recorded requested extension of H.6, not a declaration found in the baseline or a theorem explicitly stated in H.6’s present atlas text.
proofSteps: Use GeneralAlgebraicKTheory:K.1/elementary-properties-of-K-groups for the multiplication induced by exact direct sum. H.1 supplies realization/product and natural-isomorphism/homotopy comparisons; Q(P(A)) is connected through its maps from zero.
The unit, associativity and symmetry isomorphisms give the H-space properties. The connected H-space simplicity theorem is part of the explicit H.6 extension request.

Apply Serre’s finite-type theorem as requested from the homotopy supplier. Concretely, π_1 X=H_1 X is finitely generated abelian; its classifying-space homology is finitely generated. IV.3 Proposition 3 trivializes its action on universal-cover homology. III.1 Proposition 1(b), interpreted on the covering fibration over Bπ_1, makes the simply connected universal cover have finite-type homology. V.2 Proposition 1 then gives finite generation of its higher homotopy groups. The singular-complex interpretation in V.1 footnote 6 removes the original ULC regularity restriction. Use K_n=π_{n+1} BQ.
Specialize to O_F using the arithmetic inputs in the previous node. Preserve the predecessor’s endpoint IDs for consumers.
acceptance: π_1 BQ(A)=K_0(A) generally contains Z, so replacing BQ by a simply connected space is incorrect.
The homotopy shift is n+1, including K_0=π_1; positive plus-model degrees instead use π_n BGL(A)^+.
For A=Z the result is finite generation in all degrees, not finiteness of all K-groups.

sources.locator: End of proof of Theorem 1, printed p.185, PDF p.193
sources.match: Quillen passes from finite integral homology to homotopy using the H-space structure.

nodes.title: Finite kernel and cokernel for finite-S localization
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field, A=O_F, S a finite set of nonzero prime ideals of A, and B=O_{F,S}. For every n≥2, K_n(A) → K_n(B) has finite kernel and finite cokernel. It is injective for positive even n and surjective for odd n≥3. Consequently K_n(B) is finitely generated for n≥2; degree one is finitely generated via the retained K1 determinant/S-unit comparison and finite S, and degree zero via the retained K0/class-group comparison. This refines finite-generation-of-K-of-S-integers, whose ID remains the target endpoint.
hypotheses: The maps are the functorial K maps under A→B, and finite defect concerns their actual kernels/cokernels.
Use the predecessor presentation of S-integers as a localization; A itself is finite over Z, whereas B generally is not.
Each residue field A/p is finite. Finite S is required in degrees ≥1.
proofSteps: Use N.1/S-integers-localisation-of-torsion-class-group to choose nonzero s with B=A[1/s] and the primes containing s exactly S: take the product of generators of positive principal powers of the primes in S, and s=1 for S empty. Apply the finite localization sequence and dévissage in N.2/finite-support to obtain ⊕_{p∈S}K_n(A/p) → K_n(A) → K_n(B) → ⊕_{p∈S}K_{n−1}(A/p). This is the sequence for A → B, not a restriction of the fraction-field sequence. Use exactness to express the kernel as an image and the cokernel as a subgroup.

Quillen’s finite-field table (KTheoryFiniteLocalFields:L.1/quillen-k-groups) makes the two outer terms finite for n≥2. Its positive even groups vanish: the left term is zero for even n, and the right term is zero for odd n≥3.

An image of a finitely generated abelian group is finitely generated and a finite cokernel is finitely generated; the baseline exact-sequence lemma proves finite generation of the middle target using quillen-homotopy-finite-type.

For n=1 the right outer term is Z^S, not finite. Use the imported K1 identification with units and Tau Ceti’s finite-S unit theorem instead. K0 is Z plus a finite class group quotient; do not extrapolate the finite-defect assertion to degree one.
acceptance: For S empty the map is the identity, with zero kernel and cokernel.
For B=Z[1/p], the degree-one cokernel on units is Z; it is finitely generated but infinite.
If all rational primes are inverted, B=Q and K1(Q)=Q× is not finitely generated; no infinite-S conclusion is stated.
For even n≥2 injectivity follows from vanishing K_n(residue), not from a torsion-free assertion about K_n(A).

sources.match: The finite-field localization calculation gives finite defects in n>1 and even-degree injectivity.

gaps.title: Missing carriers prevent full signature elaboration
gaps.detail: Pinned libraries do not provide the Q-rank spaces, building/Steinberg coefficient carriers, relative comparison package or higher Quillen K-group carrier. The suggested file therefore has a comment-only intended signature register for these five names and compiled Mathlib examples for the existing arithmetic/algebra inputs; no opaque stand-ins or placeholder proposition fields are introduced. Convert the register to elaborated signatures once suppliers are available. Tau Ceti baseline statements were read, but not elaborated against a newer shared checkout. Independent review: this accurately records the missing carriers, but a comment-only register does not satisfy PROTOCOL section 13, which requires the named theorems as actual Lean declarations with prototype proofs. Supply truthful typed prototypes, with unstateable conditions explicitly omitted as the protocol permits, and reconcile the reader with the corrected finite-S supplier chain. No opaque carrier or proposition-field substitutes are permitted.
